module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 770

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/770](https://www.erdosproblems.com/770)
 - [Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical
    Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
 - [Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal,
    Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set ENat Filter

namespace Erdos770


/-- Let $h n$ be the minimal number such that $2 ^ n - 1, \dots, h(n) ^ n - 1$
are collectively coprime. -/
noncomputable def h (n : ℕ) : ℕ∞ := sInf {m | 2 < m ∧
  ((Finset.Icc 2 m.toNat).image fun i => (i ^ n - 1)).gcd id = 1}

/-- `n + 1` is prime iff `h n = n + 1`. This is described as 'easy to see' in [Er74b]. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem Nat.Prime.h_eq_add_one {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 < n) : h n = n + 1 ↔ (n + 1).Prime := by
  sorry

/-- For odd `n`, the values of `h n` form an unbounded set.
This is described as 'easy to see' in [Er74b]. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.variants.odd_h_unbounded : Unbounded (· ≤ ·) (ENat.toNat '' (h '' Odd)):= by
  sorry


/-- For every prime `p`, does the density of integers with `h n = p` exist? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ a, HasDensity {n | h n = p} a := by
  sorry

/-- Does `liminf h n = ∞`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ liminf h atTop = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/-- Is it true that if `p` is the greatest prime such that `p - 1 ∣ n` and `p > n ^ ε`, then
`h n = p`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    let p := sSup {m : ℕ | m.Prime ∧ m - 1 ∣ n}
    p > (n : ℝ) ^ (ε : ℝ) → h n = p := by
  sorry

/-- It is probably true that `h n = 3` for infinitely many `n`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.variants.three : {n | h n = 3}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos770

findings.description: The module bibliography lists [Er49d] and [Ma66], two papers on the strong law of large numbers, rather than the primary source of the number-theoretic claims stated here. The relevant paper is [Er74b], which the two textbook theorem docstrings already cite but which is missing from the bibliography. This is a reference slip; the mathematical statements are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, “Remarks on some problems in number theory,” Mathematica Balkanica 4 (1974), 197–202, §II, pp. 199–200, defines h(n) and discusses precisely the prime characterization, odd-index unboundedness, densities, large greatest eligible prime, and infinitely many h(n)=3: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1974-27.pdf. The cited 1949 and 1966 papers instead concern almost-everywhere convergence of sums of periodic functions along lacunary sequences.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Er49d] and [Ma66] bibliography entries with [Er74b]: P. Erdős, “Remarks on some problems in number theory,” Mathematica Balkanica 4 (1974), 197–202, especially §II, pp. 199–200. Retain the erdosproblems.com reference.

reformulations.difference: Lean minimizes over endpoints m > 2 and uses ℕ∞ to totalize the definition. A literal least-integer convention allowing m = 2 gives h(1)=2, whereas Lean gives h(1)=3; Lean also assigns h(0)=⊤.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n≥2, the endpoint m=2 cannot qualify: its gcd is 2^n−1≥3. Thus the minima agree for every n≥2. I proved this agreement and finiteness of Lean h(n) for every positive n in scratch Lean. The possible discrepancy at n=1 changes level sets by at most one element, preserving density existence, infinitude, limits, and odd-index unboundedness. The textbook characterization assumes n>2; its omitted positive boundary cases under the literal minimum convention are directly true. Consequently no claim in the file changes. The complete collection of finite-perturbation equivalences was not formalized.

review.notes: Reviewed the definition and all six theorem statements. No mathematical misformalization was found, and the source still records the problem as OPEN. Scratch files under /workspace/review/ compile successfully and verify h(0)=⊤, h(1)=h(2)=3, finiteness for positive inputs, the greatest-prime interpretation of sSup for n>0, and the equivalence of ENat liminf=⊤ with eventually exceeding every finite bound. Computations found no violation of the textbook prime characterization for 3≤n≤100. The liminf question uses an unresolved answer slot, so its coexistence with the conjecture of infinitely many h(n)=3 is not a defect.
